title: Synergistic Effects of Gibberellic Acid, Forchlorfenuron, Thidiazuron, and Brassinosteroid Combinations on Seedless Berry Development and Quality Enhancement in 'Shine Muscat' and 'Red Muscat of Alexandria' Grapes
content: Plant growth regulators (PGRs) play crucial roles in optimizing grape berry quality, yet their cultivar-specific effects and microstructural impacts remain inadequately characterized. This study systematically investigated the effects of five PGRs—gibberellic acid (GA3), 24-epibrassinolide (EBR), forchlorfenuron (CPPU), thidiazuron (TDZ), and streptomycin (SM)—on berry development and quality parameters in ’Shine Muscat’ and ’Red Muscat of Alexandria’ grape cultivars. Twelve treatment combinations were applied at full bloom (D0) and 14 days post-anthesis (D14), with comprehensive morphological, physiological, and histological analyses conducted over 104 days. Results demonstrated pronounced cultivar-specific responses to PGR treatments. In ’Shine Muscat’, GA3+TDZ and GA3+CPPU combinations achieved nearly 100% seedlessness, while CPPU and TDZ significantly enhanced berry weight and size through cortical expansion. GA3 treatment increased berry weight but induced undesirable rachis thickening and reduced total soluble solids (TSS). EBR at concentrations ≥0.2 mg/L inhibited berry growth, whereas SM reduced berry size and weight. Microstructural analysis revealed that TDZ and CPPU increased cortical area and epidermal thickness, enhancing pericarp robustness and potentially improving disease resistance. GA3 significantly increased vascular bundle area, supporting its role in vascular tissue development. In contrast, ’Red Muscat of Alexandria’ exhibited weaker responses to most PGR treatments, suggesting inherent physiological differences between Vitis vinifera and hybrid cultivars. The study establishes that combinatorial PGR applications can synergistically optimize grape berry quality through cultivar-specific regulation of growth, metabolism, and microstructure. These findings provide a scientific foundation for precision viticulture strategies, demonstrating that TDZ and CPPU show production potential for berry enhancement, while GA3 and EBR require careful dosage optimization to balance beneficial effects with potential adverse impacts on fruit quality and structure.
